<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
A continuously differentiable function $B: \mathcal{X} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a (zeroing) Control Barrier Function (CBF) for the nominal system \eqref{eq:nominal_dyn} if there exists an extended class-$\mathcal{K}$ function $\alpha$ \cite{ames2016control} such that
    \begin{subequations}
    \begin{align}
        B(x) &< 0, \quad \forall x \in \mathcal{F}, \label{eq:cbf:sign} \\
        B(x) &\geq 0 \implies \sup_{u \in \mathcal{U}} \nabla B(x)^{\top} \bar{f}(x, u) \geq -\alpha(B(x)). \label{eq:cbf:descent}
    \end{align}
    \end{subequations}
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
For any $D>0$, let $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x) \coloneqq J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x) - D$ and $\mathcal{S}_D \coloneqq \{x : J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x) \geq 0\}$.
    Then, $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D$ is a CBF for the nominal dynamics \eqref{eq:nominal_dyn}.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Since $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}=0$ on $\mathcal F$, $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x) = -D < 0$ for all $x \in \mathcal{F}$, which satisfies the first CBF condition \eqref{eq:cbf:sign}.
    For the second condition \eqref{eq:cbf:descent}, since $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}$ is the value function of an optimal control problem, it satisfies the stationary Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman (HJB) equation \cite{bardi1997optimal} on the complement of the failure set $\mathcal{F}^\complement = \mathcal{X} \setminus \mathcal{F}$.
    \begin{align}
        0
        &= \inf_d \{ \ell(d) + \nabla J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)^{\top} f(x, \pi_{\mathrm{fb}}(x), d) \}, \\
        &\leq  \ell(0) + \nabla J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)^{\top} f(x, \pi_{\mathrm{fb}}(x), 0), \\
        &\leq \sup_u \nabla J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)^{\top} \bar{f}(x, u).
    \end{align}
    For any $x \in \mathcal{S}_D$, $\alpha(J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x)) \geq 0$. Thus,
    \begin{equation}
        \sup_u \nabla J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x)^{\top} \bar{f}(x, u) \geq 0 \geq -\alpha(J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x)),
    \end{equation}
    and the second CBF condition \eqref{eq:cbf:descent} holds.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
For a given disturbance budget $D > 0$, a system started from $x_0$ is safe under budget $D$ if it does not enter the failure set $\mathcal{F}$ for any disturbance signal $(d_t)_{t \geq 0} \in \mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{feas}}$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
\label{thm:budget}
    $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D$ certifies the safety of the set $\mathcal{S}_D$ under budget $D$ in the sense that, under the fallback policy $\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}$, all states $x_0 \in \mathcal{S}_D$ are safe under budget $D$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
If a disturbance in $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{feas}}$ causes finite-time failure at $T$ under $\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}$ from $x_0 \in \mathcal{S}_D$, it is feasible in \eqref{eq:leap_value}, giving
    \begin{equation}
        D \leq J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_0) \leq \int_0^T \ell(d_t)\,\mathop{}\!\mathrm{d} t = A_T < D,
    \end{equation}
    which is a contradiction. This also holds for $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_0) = \infty$.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
\label{thm:budget_switch}
    Suppose $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}$ is finite and continuous on $\mathcal{X}$.
    Then, every $x_0 \in \mathcal{S}_D$ is safe under budget $D$ under $\pi_{\mathrm{sw}}$.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Suppose a disturbance in $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{feas}}$ drives the switched system from $x_0 \in \mathcal{S}_D$ to $x_T \in \mathcal{F}$ at some finite time $T$.
    Since $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_T)=0<D\leqJ^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_0)$, continuity gives a last threshold crossing $s=\max\{t\in[0,T]:J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_t)=D\}$.
    On $(s,T]$, $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_t)<D$, so the filter follows $\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}$.
    The shifted disturbance $\widetilde d_t=d_{s+t}$ belongs to $\mathcal{D}_{\mathrm{feas}}$, since its accumulated effort satisfies $\widetilde A_t=A_{s+t}-A_s\leq A_{s+t}<D$ for all $t\geq0$.
    Under this disturbance, the fallback trajectory from $x_s\in\mathcal{S}_D$ reaches $x_T\in\mathcal{F}$, contradicting \Cref{thm:budget}.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:switch_qp}
    Consider the CBF-QP safety filter \eqref{eq:cbf_qp} with $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D$ as the CBF, but switching to the fallback policy $\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}$ whenever the QP is infeasible or $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}_D(x) \leq 0$.
    Call this controller $\pi_{\mathrm{sw+qp}}$.
    Then, for any $x_0 \in \mathcal{S}_D$, the system is safe under budget $D$ under this safety filter
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
\label{thm:budget_qp}
    Suppose $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}$ is finite and continuous on $\mathcal{X}$, and continuously differentiable wherever $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}>0$.
    Let $H(x,A)\coloneqqJ^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)-D+A$, with $A_t$ given by \eqref{eq:disturbance_budget}, and choose $\kappa>0$.
    Consider the filter $\pi_{\mathrm{D\text{-}safe\ qp}}(x,A)$ defined by the minimizer of
    \begin{equation}\label{eq:budget_qp}
        \begin{aligned}
\min_{u\in\mathcal{U}}\quad
            &\tfrac12\|u-\pi_{\mathrm{nom}}(x)\|^2\\
            \text{s.t.}\quad
            &\inf_{d\in\mathcal{D}}\{\nablaJ^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)^\top f(x,u,d)+\ell(d)\}\\
            &\qquad\geq-\kappa H(x,A).
        \end{aligned}
    \end{equation}
    The constraint is feasible whenever $H\geq0$ and $A<D$.
    From any $x_0\in\mathcal{S}_D$, this filter preserves $H(x_t,A_t)\geq0$ while $A_t<D$ and guarantees disturbance-budget safety.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
The fallback HJB inequality gives $\inf_d\{\nablaJ^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)^\top f(x,\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}(x),d)+\ell(d)\}\geq0$.
    Thus $u=\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}(x)$ is feasible when $H\geq0$ and $A<D$, since then $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x)>0$ and $-\kappa H\leq0$.
    Along the filtered trajectory, $\dot A_t=\ell(d_t)$ and \eqref{eq:budget_qp} imply
    \begin{equation}
        \dot H_t=\nablaJ^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_t)^\top f(x_t,u_t,d_t)+\ell(d_t)
        \geq-\kappa H_t.
    \end{equation}
    Since $H_0=J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_0)-D\geq0$, integration gives $H_t\geq e^{-\kappa t}H_0\geq0$ while $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_t)>0$ and $A_t<D$.
    By continuity, a first time with $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_t)=0$ and $A_t<D$ would give $H_t=A_t-D<0$, a contradiction.
    Hence $J^{\pi_{\mathrm{fb}}}(x_t)\geq D-A_t>0$ whenever $A_t<D$, which excludes failure.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
